headword: {卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}

definitions.explanation: A market where goods, especially fresh produce, fish, and meat, are sold in bulk to retailers and restaurants rather than directly to consumers.

examples.japanese: {築地|つきじ}は{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}として{有名|ゆうめい}だった。
examples.english: Tsukiji was famous as a wholesale market.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}、{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}で{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}を{仕入|しい}れる。
examples.english: Every morning, I stock up on fresh fish at the wholesale market.

examples.japanese: {中央|ちゅうおう}{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}は{地方自治体|ちほうじちたい}が{管理|かんり}し、{食|しょく}の{安全|あんぜん}を{支|ささ}えている。
examples.english: Central wholesale markets are managed by local governments and support food safety.

notes:
Composed of {卸売|おろしうり} (wholesale) + {市場|しじょう} (market). In Japan, {中央|ちゅうおう}{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう} (central wholesale markets) are public markets regulated by law, handling the distribution of perishable foods. The most famous example is the former {築地|つきじ}{市場|しじょう}, which moved to {豊洲|とよす} in 2018.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中央|ちゅうおう}{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}: central wholesale market
- {地方|ちほう}{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}: regional wholesale market
- {卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}で{仕入|しい}れる: to stock up at a wholesale market
- {青果|せいか}{卸売|おろしうり}{市場|しじょう}: fruit and vegetable wholesale market

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {卸売|おろしうり}: wholesale — the broader concept of selling goods in bulk
- {小売|こうり}{市場|しじょう}: retail market — where goods are sold directly to consumers
- {朝市|あさいち}: morning market — a public market open early in the morning, often for retail
